parties: <cite index="2-1">Solinas Integrity Private Limited raised $5.5 million Series A1 from Hero Enterprise Partner Ventures (lead) and Mela Ventures (co-lead), with participation from Luthra Group</cite>, and <cite index="2-2">existing investors SBI Ventures (SVL-SME Fund), Rainmatter, and 8X Ventures Fund I</cite>.
headline: <cite index="1-3">Solinas Integrity Private Limited has raised $5.5 million from a Series A1 fundraise led by Hero Enterprise Partner Ventures and co-led by Mela Ventures</cite>, with <cite index="44-1">Sequitur Advocates & Legal Consultants acting as exclusive legal advisor</cite>.
sum: IIT Madras-incubated climate deeptech and robotics startup Solinas Integrity raised $5.5 million in Series A1 led by Hero Enterprise and Mela Ventures. The company builds robotics and AI systems that inspect, clean, and digitise underground water and wastewater infrastructure, solving water leakage, contamination, and manual scavenging problems.
implication: Series A1 follow-on rounds in climate-tech deeptech-especially capital-intensive hardware-AI hybrids-benefit from investor syndication (conglomerate + VC + family office) and require crisp structuring of IP ownership, founder dilution mechanics, and government subsidy offsets (AMRUT, Jal Jeevan Mission anchoring customer demand).
detail: <cite index="2-3">The round follows Solinas's Series A, led by SBI Ventures through the SVL-SME Fund (Neev II) in May 2024.</cite> <cite index="2-4">Solinas builds robotics and AI systems that inspect, clean, and digitize underground water and wastewater infrastructure.</cite> <cite index="4-5">Its technology is currently deployed across more than 35 cities and 15 states in India; the company has also expanded to the Middle East.</cite> <cite index="18-4,18-5">Capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, product development, strengthen software infrastructure, and support working capital requirements as Solinas scales government and enterprise contracts, with government-led infrastructure programmes such as AMRUT, Jal Jeevan Mission, and the NAMASTE scheme driving adoption.</cite>

framework.note: Solinas Integrity is a Pvt Ltd; series rounds with institutional investors require compliance with shareholding restrictions and articles.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, Schedule I & RBI Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)
framework.note: Foreign investor participation (Hero Enterprise, Mela, Luthra); inbound capital must comply with FDI caps for non-sensitive sectors; deeptech hardware may trigger additional scrutiny.

framework.ref: Startup India (Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion) self-certification regime
framework.note: IIT Madras-incubated ventures qualify as recognized startups; tax exemptions and angel tax exemptions on ESOPs apply; documentation simplification.
Series A1 investment in unlisted company; exemption where investee is DPIIT-recognized startup and fair-market valuation certified by category-I merchant banker.

framework.ref: SEBI Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) Regulations, 2012, as amended
framework.note: If Mela Ventures / Hero Enterprise operate as Category II / III AIF, fundraise structuring may require GP-LP side letters on follow-on investment commitments and reserved matters.

framework.ref: RBI Forex Policy – Inbound Remittances by Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPI)
framework.note: Hero Enterprise / Mela Ventures remittance documentation for capital deployment and repatriation; deeptech hardware sector may require enhanced documentation.

framework.ref: Shareholder Agreement Provisions – founder dilution, liquidation preferences, anti-dilution, drag-along / tag-along
framework.note: Standard in institutional Series A rounds; syndication among four investor classes (lead, co-lead, tertiary, existing) complicates waterfall modeling and exit mechanics.

framework.ref: SAFE / Convertible Note documentation (if any bridge used)
framework.note: Not stated in sources; if conversion timing tied to future Series B or exit milestones, conversion discount and valuation caps are key structuring levers.

framework.ref: IIT Madras Incubation Policy & IP Assignment
framework.note: Incubation agreements typically retain IIT IP audit rights; confirm clean chain of title for robotics patents / algorithms before closing.

conditions: Institutional shareholding caps & Board seat allocation among lead (Hero), co-lead (Mela), secondary (Luthra), and existing investors (SBI, Rainmatter, 8X)
Fair-market valuation certification (implicit for angel tax exemption under §56(2)(viic))
Founder / management representations & warranties on IP provenance, regulatory compliance, undisclosed liabilities
Potential anti-dilution (broad-based or narrow-based weighted average) given multiple investor tiers
Reserved matters consent (capital expenditure, new product lines, international expansion spending)
approvals: RBI/FEMA approval for inbound foreign capital (Hero Enterprise, Mela Ventures likely US/global LPs)
Shareholder approval for issuance of new share class / CCPS (Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares) if structured as CCPS round
Board & founding shareholder consent to equity dilution
IIT Madras incubation authority sign-off on continued use of incubation infrastructure post-Series A1 (likely administrative)
structure.novel: <cite index="2-2,2-3">SBI Ventures, through the SVL-SME Fund, doubled down on its position; the round follows Solinas's Series A led by SBI Ventures in May 2024, underscoring deepening alignment between India's climate-tech innovation ecosystem and global sustainability-focused capital.</cite> Syndication of conglomerate (Hero Enterprise via Partner Ventures entity), traditional VC (Mela), and family office / group holding (Luthra) alongside repeat institutional BFSI investors reflects institutional consolidation around deeptech hardware unicorn thesis in WASH sector.

triggers.law: FEMA Liberalised Remittance Scheme & RBI FDI press notes
triggers.note: Inbound capital from overseas-domiciled investors (Hero Enterprise / Mela Ventures LPs) must satisfy FDI sectoral eligibility for manufacturing of robotics / industrial automation.
IIT Madras incubation + founding date + business sector unlock §56(2)(viic) angel tax exemption and GST/customs incentives for early-stage capital raise.
If incorporated PLC or LLP, Solinas may claim deduction for certain capex & employee remuneration; series A valuations lock in baseline for depreciation & carry-forward loss utilization.

triggers.law: SEBI (Venture Capital Fund) Regulations & AIF Regulations
triggers.note: If Mela Ventures registered as Category II AIF, reporting of follow-on investment rounds and investor-level LPAP documentation mandatory.
